mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the pattern reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals a demand recovery in consumer durables, which boosts cyclicals and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the pattern fails during a simultaneous supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals labor market overheating, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as discount rates rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the pattern inverts during a monetary easing cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings expectations for cyclicals and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the pattern fails during a simultaneous demand surge.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% combined with a concurrent rise in real savings (RSAFS) signals a deflationary environment that reduces corporate pricing power and profit margins, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL drops > 0.5pp month-over-month AND RSAFS rises > 3% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the pattern reverses during a monetary stimulus.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month average without a corresponding rise in consumption (GDPC1) signals a precautionary savings regime, which reduces near-term consumption demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA for 3 consecutive months AND GDPC1 growth < 0.2% monthly
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the pattern fails during a fiscal stimulus.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the labor force participation rate (implied by inverse of UNRATE with constant population) above 63% for six consecutive months signals a tighter labor market, which raises wage growth and input costs, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher pricing power in services and select industrials.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the pattern inverts during a simultaneous monetary tightening.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a residential construction boom, which boosts demand for materials and financials and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the pattern fails during a simultaneous rise in mortgage rates.
